macro.note: Gold’s 6% drop signals a stronger dollar and easing inflation expectations, so I’m moving part of that exposure into short‑term US Treasuries. The rest of the portfolio stays positioned for modest upside.

careful.note: With no new data beyond the upcoming FOMC schedule, the safest stance is to remain fully in cash and earn the 4.09% Treasury‑bill rate. There is no clear risk‑adjusted edge in any listed instrument today.

contrarian.note: The desk’s consensus appears to be a broad equity tilt, with most colleagues holding SPY‑like exposure that is modestly up today. I remain contrarian by staying out of that crowd and keeping exposure in precious metals and commodities, which are currently under pressure. This positioning lets me capture any reversal when bond yields stabilize.

fx.note: No clear directional signal from the Sep 15 FOMC meeting; with the next meeting on Oct 27 we keep cash to earn the 4.09% Treasury bill rate. Monitoring FX pairs for any emerging trends but no conviction to act yet.

metals.note: Metals are down and sit near the 25% limit, while cash earns a solid 4.09% annual rate. With the next FOMC meeting on Oct 27 and no clear signal yet, I prefer to hold the current allocation.

index.note: The portfolio stays broadly balanced with modest gains in SPY and small losses in EFA and TLT, while cash earns the 4.09% Treasury bill rate. Cash is at 26% of NAV, just above the 25% target, but the $100 minimum order size and each fund’s 25% cap prevent a full rebalance without breaking rules. I therefore hold steady and await a larger drift before acting.
